Rashi on Keritot 14a:10:1.english: Does one follow [the majority] with regard to limbs, etc. - This dilemma [is] in the chapter [entitled] Behemah HaMakshah (Chullin 70a).

Rashi on Keritot 14a:10:2.hebrew: כזית אחד - חלב דאיסור קמיירי, בשני זיתי חלב לא קמיירי:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:10:2.english: One olive-bulk - It is dealing [with one olive-bulk] of forbidden fat; it is not dealing with two olive-bulks of forbidden fat.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:11:1.hebrew: כותבת אית בה ב' זיתים - דכך בית הבליעה מחזיק:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:11:1.english: A large date-bulk contains two olive-bulks - For that is how much the throat holds.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:12:1.hebrew: כגון שאכל כוליא בחלבה - דאאכילת חלב מחייב שלש חטאות ואשם, וגורם נמי להשלמת אכילת כותבת, וזית של כוליא משלים לכותבת. הילכך לא תנא פגול, דבשני זיתי חלב לא קמיירי. ואי תימא: לוקים כגון שהעלה זית של כוליא אמזבח, דהוה חלב פיגול ולכוליא נותר — א"כ לא מהני נותר אזית דחלב, ואנן בעינן דליהוי חד אכולהו, דאכילה קתני, דהיינו כזית:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:12:1.english: Where he eats a kidney with its fat - For [by] eating forbidden fat, he is liable for three sin-offerings and a guilt-offering, and it also contributes to completing the eating of a date-bulk, and an olive-bulk of kidney completes [it] to a date-bulk. Therefore, [the Mishnah] did not teach piggul, because it is not speaking of two olive-bulks of forbidden fat. And if you say: Let us establish [it] in a case where he offered an olive-bulk of kidney upon the altar, so that the forbidden fat is piggul and the kidney is notar — if so, notar does not apply to the olive-bulk of forbidden fat, whereas we require that there be one [olive-bulk] for all of them, since [the Mishnah] teaches "eating," which is an olive-bulk.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:12:2.hebrew: (גליו"ן) אלא בכזית אחד מיירי, ואי אנחיה לפלגיה דזית אמזבח, אין הקטרה בפחות מכזית:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:12:2.english: (Gloss) Rather, [the Mishnah] is speaking of a single olive-bulk, and if he placed half of the olive-bulk upon the altar, there is no [valid] burning with less than an olive-bulk.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:12:3.hebrew: כגון שאכל כוליא בחלבה - ואם נפשך לומר, ליחייב אכוליא משום פיגול ואחלבה משום נותר — לא מצי למימר הכי, דטמא שאכל קתני, דבחלב עצמו בעי לאוקומי לכולהו איסורי. פירוש מורי:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:12:3.english: Where he ate a kidney with its fat - And if you should wish to say: let him be liable for the kidney on account of piggul [an offering disqualified by improper intention] and for its fat on account of notar [leftover sacrificial meat] — one cannot say this, for [the Mishnah] teaches "an impure person who ate [it]," as it must establish all of the prohibitions in the fat itself. [This is] the explanation of my teacher.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:12:4.hebrew: רב פפא אמר - להכי לא תנא פיגול, דלא מיירי בשני זיתי חלב. ודקא קשיא לך כותבת — כגון דמלייה לחלב בתמרי, והשלימו לככותבת:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:12:4.english: Rav Pappa said - For this reason [the Tanna] did not teach piggul [disqualified sacrificial meat], because [the Mishnah] is not dealing with two olive-bulks of chelev [forbidden fat]; and [as for] that which was difficult for you [regarding the measure of] a date-bulk — [it is] a case where he supplemented the chelev with dates and completed it to [the volume of] a date-bulk.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:13:1.english: And he explains it, such as where one ate an olive-bulk of piggul - From another animal together with it.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:15:1.hebrew: וניתני אם הוציאו חייב - דהא יה"כ הוא:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:15:1.english: And let [the Mishnah] teach: If he carried it out, he is liable - For it is Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:17:1.english: With one who is designated for it - [Meaning] that they designate him from the day before to lead the goat.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:18:1.hebrew: זאת אומרת - מדקתני אפילו בשבת, אין עירוב והוצאה ליה"כ. דאם יש איסור הוצאה ליה"כ, אמאי איצטריך לרבויי שבת? הא דחי יה"כ, והוא הדין לשבת:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:18:1.english: That is to say - Since it taught "even on Shabbat," [it follows that] there is no [requirement of] joining [courtyards] and [no prohibition against] carrying on Yom Kippur. For if there were a prohibition against carrying on Yom Kippur, why would it be necessary to include Shabbat? Behold, it [already] overrides Yom Kippur, and the same law [would apply] to Shabbat.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:19:1.hebrew: דילמא - מיה"כ לא שמעינן לשבת, דיה"כ שאני, דהכשר מצותו בכך, דומיא דתמידין שקריבין בשבת:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:19:1.english: Perhaps - From Yom Kippur we do not derive [the law] for Shabbat, for Yom Kippur is different, as the validity of its mitzvah is in this [manner], similar to the daily offerings that are offered on Shabbat.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:1:1.hebrew: נהי דאיסור - גרידא חל על איסור לית ליה, כגון האוכל נבלת בהמה טמאה, אינו חייב משום נבלה, דהיינו איסור גרידא דליכא לא כולל ולא מוסיף:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:1:1.english: Although [a] prohibition - [i.e.,] a mere [prohibition] takes effect upon [another] prohibition, he does not hold [this] — for example, one who eats the carcass of an impure animal is not liable on account of [eating] a carcass, for that is a mere prohibition, where there is neither an inclusive [prohibition] nor an expanded [prohibition].

Rashi on Keritot 14a:20:1.english: His daughter and his sister - For he engaged in intercourse with his mother and fathered her.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:20:2.hebrew: ואשת אחיו - שנשאת לו קודם לכן, ולאחר מיתתו נשאה אחי אביו, ובא זה, אביה, עליה בנדתה:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:20:2.english: And the wife of his brother - For she had married him previously, and after his death his father's brother married her, and this [man], her father, engaged in intercourse with her while she was a menstruant.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:2:1.hebrew: מגו דנאסר בחתיכות (טהורות) - איתסר נמי בחלב משום טומאה. והיינו כולל, דלא איתוסף איסורא אחפצא, אלא אגברא איתוסף איסורא לגבי אחריני, כייל נמי להאי באיסורא:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:2:1.english: Since he became prohibited from [eating] (pure) pieces - He also became prohibited from [eating] the forbidden fat on account of ritual impurity. And this is [the principle of] kollel [an inclusive prohibition], for a prohibition was not added to the object [itself]; rather, a prohibition was added to the person with respect to other [items], [and so] it includes this [item] as well in the prohibition.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:3:1.hebrew: איסור הנייה - היינו מוסיף, דאיתוסף איסורא אחפצא:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:3:1.english: A prohibition of [deriving] benefit - That is [a case of] mosif [an expanded prohibition], since a prohibition was added to the object.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:4:2.hebrew: יה"כ - איסור כולל, דאיתוסף איסורא אגברא אמידי דמשתרי ליה עד השתא:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:4:2.english: Yom Kippur - [It is] an inclusive prohibition, as a prohibition is added upon the person regarding something that was permitted to him until now.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:5:1.hebrew: בשתי בהמות לא מיירי ונותר ופיגול בחדא בהמה ליכא - דפיגול אינו אלא בד' עבודות של דם. הילכך, מדפגלה לא חזיא לא לאכילת אדם ולא לאכילת מזבח, הלכך לא חייל עליה נותר:
Rashi on Keritot 14a:5:1.english: It does not refer to two animals, and notar and piggul are not [found] in one animal - For piggul [is rendered] only during the four blood services. Therefore, once [the offering] has been rendered piggul, it is fit neither for human consumption nor for consumption by the altar; therefore, [the prohibition of] notar does not take effect upon it.

Rashi on Keritot 14a:6:1.english: As its piggul [status] is abrogated from it - Because the altar sanctified it through [sacrificial] service. Ulla's reason is explained in Zevachim (43a).

Rashi on Keritot 14a:9:1.hebrew: אי רובא אמזבח שדייה - לכולו אבר אמזבח, והוי כוליה נותר כו':
Rashi on Keritot 14a:9:1.english: If the majority [is] on the altar, throw it - [throw] the entire limb onto the altar, and all of it is notar, etc.

Tosafot on Keritot 14a:10:1.hebrew: תפשוט דבעי רמי בר חמא הלכו באיברים אחר הרוב - פירש בקונטרס: היינו בעיא דפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין ע.). ואינו נראה לר"ת, דמאי שייכא ההיא בעיא להך דהכא? דהתם מיירי אם יצא חציו ברוב אבר, אי הוי כילוד או לא. לכך נראה לפרש: דהיינו בעיא דפרק מזבח מקדש (זבחים פז.), דאיבעיא להו: אויר מזבח כמזבח או לא, כו'; רובו לכבש — ככבש דמי, רובו למזבח — כמזבח דמי; תפשוט דבעי רמי בר חמא: יש חיבור בעולין או לא:
Tosafot on Keritot 14a:10:1.english: "Resolve [the dilemma] that Rami bar Ḥama raised: Does one follow the majority with regard to limbs" - Rashi explained [that] this is the dilemma of the chapter [entitled] Behemah HaMaksheh (Chullin 70a). But this does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for what relevance does that dilemma have to this one here? For there, it deals with [a case where] half of [the fetus] emerged with the majority of a limb, whether it is considered as born or not. Therefore, it appears [correct] to explain that this is the dilemma of the chapter [entitled] Mizbe'ach Mekadesh (Zevachim 87a), where they raised a dilemma: Is the airspace of the altar like the altar or not, etc.; [if] its majority is toward the ramp, it is like the ramp; [if] its majority is toward the altar, it is like the altar; resolve [the dilemma] that Rami bar Ḥama raised: Is there connection among things ascending [onto the altar] or not?

Tosafot on Keritot 14a:15:1.hebrew: עירוב והוצאה לשבת - פירוש: נתערבה הוצאה עם שאר מלאכות לשבת, ולא נתערבה הוצאה עם שאר מלאכות בי"ה. לשון מורי ז"ל:
Tosafot on Keritot 14a:15:1.english: Eiruv and carrying out [apply] to Shabbat - Explanation: carrying out was combined with [the] other [prohibited] labors for Shabbat, and carrying out was not combined with [the] other [prohibited] labors on Yom Kippur. [This is] the wording of my teacher, of blessed memory.

Tosafot on Keritot 14a:16:1.hebrew: אם היה שבת והוציאו - וא"ת: מה שייך זה לענין אכילה? ויש לומר דהכי פירושו: והוציאו בפיו, דכיון שהניחו בפיו ברה"י והוציאה ברשות הרבים — מחייב משום הוצאה, דבליעתו היא הנחתו, דהא מוציא שתי אותיות וכתבן כשהוא מהלך — חייב, דכתיבתן זו היא הנחתן:
Tosafot on Keritot 14a:16:1.english: "If it was Shabbat and he carried it out" - And if you say: What does this [carrying out] have to do with the matter of eating? One can say that this is its explanation: "he carried it out" [means] in his mouth; for since he placed it in his mouth in a private domain and carried it out into a public domain, he is liable on account of carrying out, because his swallowing of it is its placing down — for [one who] takes out two letters and writes them while he is walking is liable, because their writing is their placing down.

Tosafot on Keritot 14a:19:1.hebrew: אלא דרפרם ברותא היא - ובפרק שני שעירים (יומא סו:) איתא נמי הא דהכא, ולא דחי "דילמא שאני שעיר המשתלח כו'" כדדחי הכא; אלא רגילות הוא: דברי תורה עניים במקומם ועשירים במקום אחר:
Tosafot on Keritot 14a:19:1.english: Rather, [that] of Rafram is an error [beruta] - And in the chapter [entitled] Shnei Se'irim (Yoma 66b), this [passage] from here is also found, and [the Gemara there] does not reject [it by saying], "Perhaps the scapegoat is different, etc.," as it rejects [it] here; rather, it is standard [practice]: "Words of Torah are sparse in their [own] place and rich in another place."

Tosafot on Keritot 14a:7:1.hebrew: אמר עולא קומץ פיגול כו' - ואם תאמר: אמאי לא פריך מאבר גופיה, דאמר פרק המזבח מקדש (זבחים פד. ופה:) דחשיב "שחטו חוץ לזמנו כו'", "אם עלו לא ירדו — כך אם ירדו לא יעלו", וקאמר עולא: ל"ש אלא שלא משלה בו האור, אבל משלה בו האור — אפילו ירדו יעלו; וא"כ, ש"מ דעושה לחמו של מזבח ופקע פיגולו ממנו? וי"ל דמכל מקום לא תנא ליה בהדיא כל כך דפקע פיגולו ממנו, כמו בהדיא דקומץ:
Tosafot on Keritot 14a:7:1.english: Ulla says: A handful of piggul, etc. - And if you ask: Why did [the Gemara] not challenge [this] from a limb itself, as it says in the chapter [entitled] HaMizbe'ach Mekadesh (Zevachim 84a and 85b), where it lists "if he slaughtered it outside its time, etc.," [and states,] "If they went up [onto the altar] they shall not go down; similarly, if they went down they shall not go up," and Ulla says: "They taught this only where the fire has not taken hold of it, but where the fire has taken hold of it, even if they went down they shall go up" — and if so, we learn from this that it becomes the bread of the altar and its piggul status is abrogated from it? One can answer that, nevertheless, it is not taught there as explicitly that its piggul status is abrogated from it as it is explicitly [stated] regarding the handful [of a meal offering].

Tosafot on Keritot 14a:7:2.hebrew: פקע פיגולו ממנו - במנחות הקשה רש"י פרק הקומץ (דף יד.): אמאי איצטריך קרא למעט קומץ מפיגול? תיפוק לי דלא קרב המתיר כמצותו! ותירץ: דמיירי במשלה בו האור ברובו, שהותרו השירים, כדאמרינן: קומץ מאימתי מתיר השיריים באכילה? משהוצת האור ברובו. וקשה: דא"כ (לוקים) דפקע פיגולו ממנו, כדמוכח הכא! ויש לומר: דמיירי שחציו העלה ע"ג המזבח וחציו לא העלה, דלא פקע פיגולו מן החצי שנשאר. ואם תאמר: ואפי' לכתחלה נמי מעלין ליה, כדאמרינן פרק בית שמאי (זבחים מג:): "האי קומץ דפלגיה אנחיה אארעא אסיקנא ליה לכתחלה"! וי"ל: שאני התם שהיה כולו מתחלה ע"ג המזבח, ואח"כ הוריד חציו למטה; אבל הכא לא היה על המזבח. וא"ת: מנחת נסכים ומנחת כהן משיח שהם כולן כליל, אמאי צריך קרא למעט אותם מפיגול? והלא אינה מתרת שום דבר! ויש לומר: כיון שקדשו בכלי, הוי כמו קרבו מתירין, וקבעה בפיגול, ולכך צריך קרא למעט:
Tosafot on Keritot 14a:7:2.english: Its piggul status has been abrogated - In Menachot, in the chapter [entitled] HaKometz (14a), Rashi raised a difficulty: Why is a verse needed to exclude a handful [of a meal offering] from [liability for] piggul? Let it be derived [from the fact] that the permitting agent was not offered in accordance with its mitzvah! And he answered: That it is referring to [a case] where the fire took hold of the majority of it, so that the remainder [of the meal offering] became permitted, as we say: From when does the handful permit the remainder for consumption? From when the fire has been ignited in the majority of it. And this is difficult: For if so [(lokim)], its piggul status has been abrogated, as is proven here! And one can say: That it is referring to [a case] where he brought half of it up onto the altar and half of it he did not bring up, for its piggul status has not been abrogated from the half that remained. And if you will say: Even initially we also bring it up, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (Zevachim 43b): "[Regarding] this handful, half of which one placed on the ground, we bring it up initially"! And one can say: There it is different, because all of it was initially on the altar, and afterward he brought half of it down below; whereas here, [that half] was not on the altar. And if you will say: A meal offering of libations and the meal offering of the anointed priest, which are entirely burned [on the altar], why is a verse needed to exclude them from piggul? After all, it does not permit anything! And one can say: Since they were sanctified in a [service] vessel, it is considered as if their permitting agents were offered, and it establishes it as piggul, and therefore a verse is needed to exclude [them].
